title: Avalanche Developer Community Call: Dynamic Fee Mechanism for Subnet-EVM (ACP 224)
description:
This Avalanche Developer Community Call covers ACP-224, which proposes introducing ACP-176–based dynamic gas limits and fee mechanics into Subnet-EVM, along with an optional ACP224FeeManagerPrecompile that enables dynamic, on-chain configuration of gas targets and fee parameters.

ACP-224 replaces the legacy Subnet-EVM windower-based fee mechanism with a capacity-based dynamic fee model, aligning Subnet-EVM with Coreth (C-Chain) and providing deterministic gas capacity bounds. This upgrade is a functional prerequisite for enabling ACP-194 (SAE) on Subnet-EVM–based L1s and reduces long-term maintenance by unifying EVM fee logic across Avalanche.

The proposal introduces:
- Dynamic gas capacity and pricing based on ACP-176
- New configurable fee parameters (targetGas, minGasPrice, maxCapacityFactor, timeToDouble)
- Genesis-based configuration and optional dynamic updates
- A new ACP224FeeManagerPrecompile for admin-controlled fee configuration post-activation
- Validator-preference–based dynamic gas target adjustment

Avalanche is a high-performance blockchain platform designed for builders who need to scale. Engineered with a revolutionary three-part Layer 1 (L1) architecture, Avalanche is anchored by its Avalanche Consensus Mechanism, ensuring near-instant finality for transactions. The platform also features an open-source Layer 0 (L0) framework, enabling the seamless creation of interoperable Layer 1 blockchains with high throughput on both public and private networks.

Supported by a global community of developers and validators, Avalanche offers a fast, low-cost environment for building the next generation of decentralized applications (dApps). With its unique blend of speed, flexibility, and scalability, Avalanche is the preferred choice for innovators pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology.

potential_elements.text: Avalanche Developer Community Call: Dynamic Fee Mechanism for Subnet-EVM (ACP 224)

This Avalanche Developer Community Call covers ACP-224, which proposes introducing ACP-176–based dynamic gas limits and fee mechanics into Subnet-EVM, along with an optional ACP224FeeManagerPrecompile that enables dynamic, on-chain configuration of gas targets and fee parameters. ACP-224 replaces the legacy Subnet-EVM windower-based fee mechanism with a capacity-based dynamic fee model, aligning Subnet-EVM with Coreth (C-Chain) and providing deterministic gas capacity bounds. This upgrade is a functional prerequisite for enabling ACP-194 (SAE) on Subnet-EVM–based L1s and reduces long-term maintenance by unifying EVM fee logic across Avalanche. The proposal introduces: - Dynamic gas capacity and pricing based on ACP-176 - New configurable fee parameters (targetGas, minGasPrice, maxCapacityFactor, timeToDouble) - Genesis-based configuration and optional dynamic updates - A new ACP224FeeManagerPrecompile for admin-controlled fee configuration post-activation - Validator-preference–based dynamic gas target adjustment Avalanche is a high-performance blockchain platform designed for builders who need to scale. Engineered with a revolutionary three-part Layer 1 (L1) architecture, Avalanche is anchored by its Avalanche Consensus Mechanism, ensuring near-instant finality for transactions. The platform also features an open-source Layer 0 (L0) framework, enabling the seamless creation of interoperable Layer 1 blockchains with high throughput on both public and private networks. Supported by a global community of developers and validators, Avalanche offers a fast, low-cost

environment for building the next generation of decentralized applications (dApps). With its unique blend of speed, flexibility, and scalability, Avalanche is the preferred choice for innovators pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology. This Avalanche Developer Community Call covers ACP-224, which proposes introducing ACP-176–based dynamic gas limits and fee mechanics into Subnet-EVM, along with an optional ACP224FeeManagerPrecompile that enables dynamic, on-chain configuration of gas targets and fee parameters. ACP-224 replaces the legacy Subnet-EVM windower-based fee mechanism with a capacity-based dynamic fee model, aligning Subnet-EVM with Coreth (C-Chain) and providing deterministic gas capacity bounds. This upgrade is a functional prerequisite for enabling ACP-194 (SAE) on Subnet-EVM–based L1s and reduces long-term maintenance by unifying EVM fee logic across Avalanche. The proposal introduces: - Dynamic gas capacity and pricing based on ACP-176 - New configurable fee parameters (targetGas, minGasPrice, maxCapacityFactor, timeToDouble) - Genesis-based configuration and optional dynamic updates - A new ACP224FeeManagerPrecompile for admin-controlled fee configuration post-activation - Validator-preference–based dynamic gas target adjustment Avalanche is a high-performance blockchain platform designed for builders who need to scale. Engineered with a revolutionary three-part Layer 1 (L1) architecture, Avalanche is anchored by its Avalanche Consensus Mechanism, ensuring near-instant finality for transactions. The platform also features an open-source Layer 0 (L0) framework, enabling the seamless creation of interoperable Layer 1 blockchains with high throughput on both public and private networks. Supported by a global community of developers and validators, Avalanche offers a fast, low-cost

environment for building the next generation of decentralized applications (dApps). With its unique blend of speed, flexibility, and scalability, Avalanche is the preferred choice for innovators pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology.
